source.title: The reviewing of object files: Object-specific integration of information.

confidence_rationale: The foundational empirical demonstration of the object file: a temporary, token-instance episodic buffer that links successive states of THE SAME object across time and motion. The object-specific preview benefit (faster naming when prime and target are bound to one continuing object) is exactly the minimal across-time entity-persistence buffer MECH-045 posits. Robust (7 experiments, 203 subjects, ~2148 citations) and the mapping to MECH-045 is near-literal -- 'object file' is the term of art MECH-045 borrows. Held below 0.9 because the paradigm is visual psychophysics in humans, whereas MECH-045 must instantiate the buffer in a latent-stack agent, and the object file here is purely token-instance whereas REE's live z_object lineage is type-level (the gap the pull was commissioned to expose).
failure_signatures: The object file is strictly TOKEN-instance (this object, this episode); it provides no account of type/category abstraction, which is where REE's live z_resource/z_object lineage actually operates -- so this paper grounds the buffer REE does NOT yet have, not the one it has.

Object-specific benefit is fragile: it requires perceived spatiotemporal continuity of a single object; when continuity cues are removed the benefit collapses, so a REE object-file buffer cannot be a free-floating key-value store -- persistence must be gated on a continuity computation REE does not currently run.

Demonstrated for a single reviewed object across a brief preview-target interval; it does not establish persistence across long occlusions or many concurrent objects (Pylyshyn/Scholl entries cover capacity and occlusion).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Information about an object is stored in a temporary episodic representation -- an 'object file' -- indexed by the object's spatiotemporal continuity rather than its features or its identity; a target is named faster if it is perceived as a new state of the same object that earlier contained a matching prime (the object-specific preview benefit).
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-045 posits 'object-file-like buffers' that bind features across time and motion to give minimal entity persistence without symbolic labels. Kahneman/Treisman/Gibbs is the source of that exact construct and supplies the behavioural signature (object-specific integration indexed by continuity, not by label) that a REE object-file buffer should reproduce. It also grounds ARC-006's 'persistent, bindable structures' clause: the file is the persistent bindable structure.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The biological object file is TOKEN-instance and continuity-indexed; REE's implemented z_object/z_resource is TYPE-level and tag-indexed. So this paper grounds the REPRESENTATION MECH-045 describes but simultaneously marks the design fork the memo flags -- to honour the object-file construct REE must add a token-keyed, continuity-gated buffer, not reuse the type-tag store. Transfer from human visual psychophysics to a latent-stack agent is non-trivial.
mapping.source_context: Human visual psychophysics; preview-target letter-naming and same/different tasks with moving framed objects; 7 experiments, 203 college students.

confidence_components.notes: Landmark, heavily replicated. High mapping fidelity because MECH-045 borrows the construct verbatim; transfer_risk elevated by the token-vs-type mismatch and human-to-agent gap.
